record.what_it_does: Hosted ecommerce platform with merchant storefronts, catalog, orders, and headless APIs.
record.auth_notes: Most REST/GraphQL Admin calls use an OAuth-derived access token in the X-Auth-Token header. Store-level API accounts give a static token. App-level accounts use a grant-code OAuth flow with one token per installing store. Account-level tokens are used for the Account API. Other methods: Storefront JWT bearer tokens, the Payments API PAT token, Customer Login JWTs, and deprecated legacy basic auth. The Store Management MCP uses OAuth 2.1 with PKCE.
record.access_notes: A store owner can create a store-level API account in their own store at no extra cost, but the store needs a BigCommerce plan or trial. Partner sandbox stores for app development come through the Partner Portal. The docs I read don't say whether sandboxes are free. Building and testing an app-level OAuth app is self-serve in the Developer Portal. Listing publicly in the App Marketplace needs BigCommerce review, but private or unlisted installs don't appear to need it. I didn't confirm the exact rules for either.
record.api_breadth_notes: Catalog, orders, customers, carts, checkouts, inventory, themes, channels, pricing, metafields, payments, B2B Edition, and the Account API. REST V2 and V3, GraphQL Storefront and Admin. Well over 50 operations.
record.mcp_notes: Store Management MCP at https://api.bigcommerce.com/mcp, or https://api.bigcommerce.com/stores/{store_hash}/mcp for one store. It is in early access, uses OAuth 2.1 with PKCE, and the store owner must enable it. A per-storefront Storefront MCP is generally available. A docs-only MCP is at https://docs.bigcommerce.com/_mcp/server. Community servers also exist.
record.blocker_notes: A public OAuth app listed for any merchant to install needs App Marketplace approval. A toolkit can still use per-merchant OAuth apps or store-level tokens without it.

evidence.quote: The `X-Auth-Token` header uses access tokens to authenticate requests.
Each store that installs the app gets its own access token through a grant code flow.
Webhooks notify applications when specific events occur on a BigCommerce store.
Store Management MCP is in early access and available to all stores.
Sandbox stores are intended for developing and testing apps.

record.needs_human: Confirm that sandbox stores are free and that unlisted OAuth apps can be installed without Marketplace review. The pricing page and the approval-requirements page weren't opened. The GitHub OpenAPI evidence comes only from a search-result summary, not a fetched page.
